column1: # Whole-genome reference source, one row per target (code/analysis/17..19).
# WHY GENOMES. Several of the loci that actually resolve these genera --
# Rickettsia sca4 and the 17 kDa antigen, Coxiella icd / dnaK / IS1111,
# Francisella sdhA, everything in Rickettsiella and Midichloria -- have almost
# no standalone gene records in GenBank. The named species that carry them
# exist only inside complete genomes. Step 18 blasts the locus out of each
# genome exactly as step 13 blasts it out of a contig, so one genome download
# per target supplies a reference for EVERY locus of that target.
# The set is fetched once and cached under results/markers/trees/refs/genome/.
# Fetching is the slow part of the workflow -- a Rickettsia genome is ~1.3 Mb
# and this table asks for tens of them -- so keep n_genomes modest and let the
# per-organism cap in config trees.curate spend it on breadth of species.
# For the piroplasms and Hepatozoon the "genome" is the MITOCHONDRIAL genome
# (~6-8 kb), which is where cox1 and cytb live. For the viruses it is the
#   target      must match a `target` in metadata/target_markers.tsv
#   n_genomes   how many records to keep (after the per-organism cap)
#   query       Entrez nuccore term; ' ||| ' separates fallbacks
# A target with no row here simply has no genome tier; its references come from
